summary.short: Prohibits financial institutions and lenders, insurers, and health care providers from discriminating against members of protected classes through use of automated decision systems, deeming a system discriminatory if it selects protected-class members at a disproportionate rate. Takes effect on the first day of the third month after enactment.
summary.long: As introduced, the bill would supplement the New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (P.L.1945, c.169). Section 1 defines 'automated decision system' as a computational process, including one derived from machine learning, statistics, or other data processing or artificial intelligence techniques, that makes a decision or facilitates human decision making, and defines 'health care provider' and 'member of a protected class' by reference to listed characteristics. Sections 2 to 4 bar a person, bank, banking organization, credit reporting agency, mortgage company or other financial institution, lender or credit institution involved in making or purchasing loans; an insurance company licensed, registered or authorized under New Jersey law; and a health care provider from discriminating through the use of an automated decision system against members of a protected class. Each section deems a system discriminatory where it selects protected-class members for participation or eligibility, or in setting rates, terms or conditions, at a rate disproportionate to the rate for non-members. Section 5 makes a violation unlawful discrimination and a violation of section 11 of P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-12). Section 6 sets the effective date as the first day of the third month next following enactment. The bill does not set out separate penalties or an enforcing authority.},

relations.note: The title says the act supplements this law. Sec. 5 makes a violation of the act a violation of its section 11 (C.10:5-12). Sec. 1 also refers to section 11 in defining 'member of a protected class'.

evidence.quote: A violation of this act shall be unlawful discrimination and a violation of section 11 of P.L.1945, c.169 (C.10:5-12).

relations.note: The definition of 'health care provider' includes health care facilities licensed under this law.

evidence.quote: a health care facility licensed pursuant to P.L.1971, c.136 (C.26:2H-1 et seq.)

relations.note: The definition of 'health care provider' refers to professions regulated under Title 45.

evidence.quote: whose professional practice is regulated pursuant to Title 45 of the Revised Statutes

notes: Text is the introduced bill (metadata: introduced, pending); no amendment or repeal of existing law is marked on its face. Target instrument IDs are left empty because no registry IDs were available. The act does not define 'discriminate' separately; Secs. 2 to 4 define discrimination only by a disproportionate selection rate test. Effective date (Sec. 6) is the first day of the third month after enactment.

events.date_text: This act shall take effect on the first day of the third month next following enactment.

evidence.quote: This act shall take effect on the first day of the third month next following enactment.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff was found. Sections 2 to 4 apply a comparative test (selection of protected-class members 'at a rate that is disproportionate' to the rate for non-members), which is not a number. Section 6 sets an effective date, which is recorded as an event rather than a threshold. Section 1 definitions contain no numeric values.
